stem: The original meaning of the word 'Vihar' is -
expl: The residence of Buddhist monks is called a Vihar (monastery). In ancient Sanskrit, Prakrit and Pali literature, there is no mention of any region named Bihar. Toward the end of the 12th century, due to the large number of Buddhist viharas in this region (especially around Odantapuri), it came to be called Vihar, which later became Bihar.

stem: Who used the caves of Barabar as their shelter-house?
expl: In the Mauryan period, the art of carving caves to make dwellings developed. During the time of Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha, shelters were carved out in the Barabar and Nagarjuni hills for the followers of the Ajivakas sect.

stem: Mahabodhi Temple has been built at Bodh Gaya where-

options.label: c
options.text: Gautama Buddha gave his first sermon

expl: At Bodh Gaya, after six years of penance, Buddha attained enlightenment at the age of 35 on the night of Vaishakh Purnima under a peepal tree. Construction of the temple at this site was started by Emperor Ashoka in the third century BCE; however, its present form was built in the 5th–6th century CE. This temple is entirely made of bricks. In 2002, UNESCO included it in the list of World Heritage Sites.

stem: Chandragupta’s palace situated at Pataliputra is mainly made up of –
expl: Excavations at Bulandibagh and Kumrahar near Patna (Pataliputra) in Bihar have revealed remains of huge wooden buildings of the Mauryan period. The credit for bringing these to light goes to Mr. Spooner. Bulandibagh yielded remains of the city fortification, while Kumrahar yielded remains of the royal palace.

stem: Which is the oldest church in Bihar?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Padri ki Haveli, also known as St. Mary’s Church, is the oldest church in Bihar. It was originally built in Patna in 1713. Its present structure was constructed in 1772.

stem: Which is the unique festival of Bihar?
expl: Chhath Puja is the most important festival of Bihar, and it is called the Mahaparv of Bihar. It is observed on the sixth day of the bright fortnight of the Kartik month, exactly six days after Diwali. On this festival, Surya Dev (Sun God) and Chhathi Maiya are worshipped, and Arghya is offered—first at sunset and the second at sunrise. Diwali, also called the festival of lights, is a major Hindu festival celebrated on the new moon day of the Kartik month. Vishu is the traditional New Year festival of Kerala. It is celebrated on the first day of the Malayalam month Medam and is considered a symbol of good luck for the coming year. Vinayak Chaturthi is celebrated by Hindus across India, including Maharashtra, on the Shukla Chaturthi of the month of Bhadrapada on the occasion of Lord Vinayak’s (Ganesha’s) birth.

stem: 'Surya Temple' is situated in which of the following cities?
expl: Surya Temple is situated in Deo (Aurangabad district). It is believed that the famous Chhath festival of Bihar began from the pond situated in front of the Sun Temple.

stem: In the context of Indian handicrafts, what is ‘Sujini’ in Bihar?
expl: In the context of Indian handicrafts, ‘Sujini’ is a type of embroidery, which has also received a GI tag. Sujini embroidery is also known as Sujani. It originated from Bhusura village in Bihar. Notably, it was initially considered a form of making quilts and blankets, in which old saris and dhotis were used as a creative canvas. The cloth was folded three or four times, and then simple stitches were applied on the used fabrics to give them a new look.

stem: In which district of Bihar, the world's tallest (251 m) statue of Mother Sita will be constructed?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: On 13 February, 2022, the National Coordinator of the Ramayan Research Council and Mahamandaleshwar of the Juna Akhara, Swami Virendranand Ji Maharaj, announced the installation of the world’s tallest statue (251 feet) of Mata Sita at Sitamarhi. Along with the statue, a digital museum, a research institute, and a study center based on the life of Mata Sita will also be constructed. Note—The Ramayan Research Council has shown the height of the statue as 251 feet in its gallery, whereas some sources have erroneously mentioned its height as 251 meters.

stem: 'Nava Nalanda Mahavihara' is famous for what?
expl: ‘Nava Nalanda Mahavihara’ is a modern center of Buddhist studies, which was established by the Government of Bihar in 1951 at Nalanda. A large number of students from Sri Lanka, Japan, Korea, Tibet, Bhutan, and other countries/ regions come here for research in Pali and Buddhist studies.
